settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: getCanonicalName strips leading directory separators before exposure (JakartaMultiPartRequest lines 329-339), reducing path-traversal abuse

In LocalizedTextUtil.findText the translateVariables pass is applied to the resolved bundle text rather than to the args in the specific overload observed, so re-evaluation of the filename is not proven for every call site
LocalizedMessage.equals/hashCode only compare stored fields and perform no formatting or evaluation
candidates.description: In JakartaMultiPartRequest, uploaded file items are constructed with the client-supplied name. getFileNames() derives the displayed name from the FileItem getCanonicalName(), which only strips leading path separators and does not neutralize expression delimiters such as %{...} or ${...} (lines 329-339). buildErrorMessage stores the exception message as the localized default message (lines 116-120), and the file/message argument objects are then exposed to the interceptor layer via getErrors(), which returns LocalizedMessage objects holding the original args. In Struts, localization utilities such as LocalizedTextUtil.findText resolve bundle text and pass message text through TextParseUtil.translateVariables, which evaluates OGNL-style expressions. If any multipart-derived name or field name reaches a message-formatting sink that applies translateVariables (for example ValidatorSupport message building), a crafted upload filename could be evaluated as an expression. Root cause: an attacker-controlled multipart filename reaches a message/argument sink without neutralizing expression metacharacters. Note: within the read spans the filename-to-argument linkage is clear, but the final evaluation sink is not in the read evidence, so this is a candidate, not a confirmed vulnerability.
missing_evidence: The JSP/tag or template that outputs action errors/messages: whether it applies expression evaluation to the already-formatted message string
Source of FileUploadInterceptor (not in the read set), which consumes getErrors() and passes args to findText
An end-to-end runtime trace from multipart filename to an actual evaluation sink
preconditions: Application exposes an action accepting multipart/form-data uploads and renders the resulting action errors/messages through the standard Struts message path that applies expression evaluation
Attacker can control the multipart filename or form field name in the upload request
candidates.title: Multipart upload filename flows into localized error-message argument and may be expression-evaluated by the message rendering path

counter_evidence: findText uses the bundled text for the translateVariables pass when the key resolves; the passed default message is only a fallback
The catch blocks log a warning and add a localized error; no direct evaluation occurs inside buildErrorMessage
candidates.description: buildErrorMessage constructs the bundle key from the exception class simple name and stores e.getMessage() as the default message (JakartaMultiPartRequest lines 83-120). In catch-all handling the exception may arise while parsing attacker-influenced multipart content, so the default message string can embed portions of attacker data. That value is retained by LocalizedMessage and later resolved by LocalizedTextUtil.findText. This is a weaker, more speculative lead than the filename flow: within the read spans it is not shown that the default message (as opposed to resolved bundle text) is ever passed to the expression-evaluating translateVariables path during rendering.
missing_evidence: Whether defaultMessage (rather than bundle text) is ever passed to translateVariables during rendering
Concrete, demonstrated attacker control over the exception message content
preconditions: Multipart parsing throws an exception whose message embeds attacker-influenced content
The error is rendered through a path that applies expression evaluation to the resolved/default text
candidates.title: Multipart error default message derived from parser exception text carried into localized message
